quizzes.title: Why Semiconductors Matter: MCQ
quizzes.passage:
Semiconductors are fundamental to modern technological systems, and they are built into a wide range of products. Automobiles and healthcare equipment are two of the areas that depend on them, and consumer electronics relies on them as well. Because so much of modern life depends on these components, their availability shapes how resilient digital and industrial supply chains can be. Semiconductor materials have an electrical conductivity that falls between that of conductors and insulators, which is what makes them useful in electronic devices.

Chip design has advanced to the point where a single chip can hold billions of transistors packed into an extremely small area. The most advanced processors use very fine manufacturing technology and can integrate a very large number of transistors. Such capability supports demanding workloads and advanced digital applications. The electronics industry that these chips serve is very large, and semiconductors form part of its base in modern technology.

The way production is organised has also been questioned. Past disruptions showed how much risk comes from relying on a small number of places for supply. In response, many governments have looked for ways to build their own chip-making strength and to draw components from a wider set of sources.

questions.q: According to the booklet, which of the following sectors is one where semiconductors are widely used?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists aerospace among the sectors where semiconductors are widely used.

questions.q: According to the booklet, the global electronics industry is valued at approximately how many trillion US dollars?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the value of the global electronics industry as approximately USD 4.3 trillion.

questions.q: Which pair of materials is given in the booklet as examples of semiconductors?
questions.explanation: The booklet names silicon and germanium as examples of semiconductor materials.

questions.q:
Consider the following two statements.
Assertion (A): Availability of semiconductor components directly influences the resilience of digital and industrial supply chains.
Reason (R): Semiconductors are used in automobiles, healthcare, defence, aerospace, telecommunications and consumer electronics.
Select the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the list of uses does not explain why component availability affects supply chain resilience.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Leading-edge 3-nanometre processors   ->   A. Materials with conductivity between conductors and insulators
II. Global electronics industry   ->   B. Vulnerabilities from concentrated supply chains
III. Silicon and germanium   ->   C. Tens of billions of transistors
IV. COVID-19 pandemic   ->   D. Approximately USD 4.3 trillion
questions.explanation: Leading-edge processors match tens of billions of transistors, the electronics industry matches USD 4.3 trillion, silicon and germanium match semiconductor materials, and COVID-19 matches supply chain vulnerabilities.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Semiconductors are used in automobiles, healthcare, defence, aerospace, telecommunications and consumer electronics.
II. Modern chips can contain billions of transistors within extremely small areas.
III. Materials with conductivity greater than conductors are called semiconductors.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement III is wrong because semiconductor materials have conductivity between conductors and insulators, not greater than conductors.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Modern chips can contain billions of transistors within extremely small areas.
II. COVID-19 exposed vulnerabilities arising from dispersion of global semiconductor supply chains.
III. Leading-edge processors based on 3-nanometre technology can integrate tens of billions of transistors.
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the booklet says COVID-19 exposed vulnerabilities from concentration, not dispersion, in supply chains.

questions.q: In nanometres, what is the technology node of the leading-edge processors described in the booklet? (number only)
questions.explanation: The booklet says leading-edge processors are based on 3-nanometre technology.

questions.q: Semiconductors form a foundational layer of which broader value chain? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes semiconductors as a foundational layer of the broader technology value chain.

questions.q: Which global event exposed vulnerabilities from concentration in semiconductor supply chains? (short name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the COVID-19 pandemic exposed vulnerabilities arising from concentration in global semiconductor supply chains.

questions.q: What is the approximate value, in trillion US dollars, of the global electronics industry? (number only)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the global electronics industry as approximately USD 4.3 trillion.

questions.q: Which material, with conductivity between conductors and insulators, is named alongside germanium? (one word)

questions.q: Besides high-performance computing, which advanced field is named as a use for such chip capabilities? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says such capabilities support high-performance computing and artificial intelligence.

questions.q: Countries have sought to develop which kind of semiconductor capabilities and diversify their sources? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says countries have sought to develop domestic semiconductor capabilities and diversify sources.

quizzes.title: SEMICON India and the Programme: MCQ
quizzes.passage:
SEMICON India is a conference and exhibition that showcases India's semiconductor capabilities. It gives the sector one place to display its progress, and each edition is an occasion to present the work done in chip-related fields. The event is staged alongside the national effort to build a domestic base for chips, which the government has pursued through a dedicated programme. Its organisation involves the India Semiconductor Mission, which serves as the nodal body for the schemes in this area. The gathering brings together displays of work from across the sector, which makes it a useful window into the country's chip-related strengths.

The Semicon India Programme is the central scheme behind this effort. Its objective is to establish a complete set of capabilities in the country, running from the creation of designs through to the production and packaging of chips. The programme's work is grouped into several connected areas, and it also covers the training of skilled people and the support of research and new ideas.

Several projects have already been announced, with companies planning facilities in different parts of the country. Some of these projects involve partnerships between Indian companies and overseas firms, and they show how the programme's goals are being turned into physical units. The projects are spread across several states and cover different stages of chip making.

questions.q: Who inaugurated SEMICON India 2026?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that PM Modi inaugurated SEMICON India 2026.

questions.q: Where was the first edition of SEMICON India held in 2022?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the first edition of SEMICON India was held in Bengaluru in 2022.

questions.q: In which year was the Semicon India Programme launched?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Semicon India Programme was launched in 2021.

questions.q:
Consider the following two statements.
Assertion (A): SEMICON India is an annual flagship conference and exhibition that showcases India's semiconductor capabilities.
Reason (R): SEMICON India is organised by the India Semiconductor Mission, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and SEMI.
Select the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the list of organisers does not explain why the event is a flagship conference.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Theme of SEMICON India 2026   ->   C. Yashobhoomi, New Delhi
II. Venue of the 2026 inauguration   ->   A. SEMI
III. Launch year of the Semicon India Programme   ->   D. Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem
IV. Co-organiser alongside the India Semiconductor Mission and MeitY   ->   B. 2021
questions.explanation: The theme is Silicon to Systems, the 2026 venue is Yashobhoomi, the programme was launched in 2021 and SEMI is the co-organiser.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Semicon India Programme was launched in 2021 to establish a complete semiconductor ecosystem in India.
II. The first edition of SEMICON India was held in Bengaluru in 2022.
III. PM Modi inaugurated SEMICON India 2026 at Dholera (Gujarat).
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement III is wrong because PM Modi inaugurated SEMICON India 2026 at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, not Dholera.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Chip design and fabrication are among the focus areas of the Semicon India Programme.
II. SEMICON India is organised by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
III. Advanced packaging is among the focus areas of the Semicon India Programme.
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the event is organised by the India Semiconductor Mission, MeitY and SEMI, not the Ministry of Commerce.

questions.q: At which New Delhi venue did PM Modi inaugurate SEMICON India 2026? (one word)

questions.q: Which Taiwanese company partnered with Tata Electronics to set up a semiconductor fab in Gujarat? (short name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Tata Electronics partnered with Power Chip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp (Taiwan) for a fab in Dholera.

questions.q: Which programme focus area concerns the training of skilled people? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists talent development among the focus areas of the Semicon India Programme.

questions.q: In which Gujarat town is the Tata Electronics semiconductor fab being set up? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Tata Electronics is establishing a semiconductor fab in Dholera (Gujarat).
